invariants: The contract is read from oodialog-web.js and oodWeb.cls at a named commit; the Qt renderer follows the page, not Windows, where the two differ and a test depends on it.
An argument on the wire never loses its own separators: 1F inside an argument travels as 1D, and an event's extra is everything after the fourth field.
A connected event that a renderer cannot produce is said so by oodWeb ("is connected but is not produced yet"); a renderer must not invent one.
The second click of a double click is a CLICK and then a DBLCLK, as the page reports it; Qt alone reports only the double click.

provenance.claim: js.cls escapes an argument's own separator.
v0.15.0 additions, including CLICK before DBLCLK.
v0.16.0 and v0.17.0 additions: month calendar, ResizingAdmin, editable combo.

summary: RENDERER_CONTRACT.md writes down what oodWeb.cls asks of a renderer, so the page (oodialog-web.js) and the Qt library can be checked against each other. There are 15 messages: setHandler, create, addControl, show, destroy, sub, op, msg, measure, screen, setMenu, popupMenu, msgBox, image and hasImage. Events come back as pageEvent(key, kind, id, code, extra), with kind CMD, NOTIFY, CTX, KEY, MSGBOX, WM, MOUSE or GC. On the flat wire, 1F separates fields and 1E separates records, and an argument's own 1F is sent as 1D, because oodWeb puts its separator inside single arguments (tree text SEP opts, a row's cells, a NOTIFY's parts). Dialog units follow Windows: fx = floor((avgWidth/26 + 1)/2)/4, fy = round(fontHeight)/8, with the font at size*96/72 pixels. The contract grows with each oodialog-wasm release; each section says which commit it was read from: GDI, images and sizing (v0.12/0.13), the mouse (v0.14), in-place editing and tab stops (v0.15), the month calendar (v0.16: mc.* ops, SELCHANGE/SELECT, GETDAYSTATE and bold days as one bit mask a month), ResizingAdmin (v0.17: ra.init with each control's four edges pinned, ra.limits, RASIZEENDED) and the editable combo's edit (v0.17: isDropList). When oodWeb.cls calls an op that oodialog-web.js answers, the Qt renderer answers it the same way, including the page's geometry where programs rely on it: list-view rows are a line and 2 px high, the header a line and 5 px, and a combo box is one line high (its cy is the height of its list).
title: The renderer contract shared with the browser page
